title: operator_inbox's invoke names cairn operator_inbox with its usage
intention: cairn/tools/operator_inbox/intention+why.json's own invoke names `cairn operator_inbox` with real usage, so the command bin/cmd/operator_inbox dispatches is documented by the component it execs.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 (Linux census, cnb under a scratch HOME): test_intent_skill.py's test_clause_2_the_five_are_named_with_real_usage is red, '`cairn operator_inbox` is not named by its own component's invoke'. a0e252bdc (2faf52fb34ca) rewrote the invoke and dropped the mention; bin/cmd/operator_inbox still execs cairn.tools.operator_inbox.inbox, and `cairn operator_inbox show artifact ad6f3d0b265c` prints the ticket.
traces_to: Law 5 (the charter beside the code says how to run it) and Law 9 (c691e19d5464's deterministic red is fixed, not explained).
how: One sentence joins the invoke through the artifact door: `cairn operator_inbox [show artifact <id>]` is the tool's own dispatcher (bin/cmd/operator_inbox), the same CLI CodeMother's show verb hands its words to. test_intent_skill.py's PROVES names this ticket on clause 2's tooth.
